newsitem.title: UK: LME ALUMINIUM HEADS BACK TOWARDS RECENT HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: LME ALUMINIUM HEADS BACK TOWARDS RECENT HIGHS.

text.p: Zinc and aluminium surged on Tuesday afternoon as short-covering and speculative buying tickled the upside, while nickel headed in the other direction, piling up more losses.
Three months aluminium ended the afternoon kerb $20.50 firmer at $1,741.50 per tonne after touching a high of $1,743.

Traders said some players went short in the morning as prices headed down, touching a low of $1,712. But it held at the lows and investment house buying during lunch sent the market into the plus column.
"I think some of the market was caught short," a trader said, who added that producer selling came in at the highs.

The cash/threes backwardation flared to $5/$10 from $3/$7 on Tuesday. Three months zinc marched up to the highest levels since prices crashed last week, hitting a high of $1,538 after earlier hitting a low of $1,505. But selling took the froth off the highs and prices ended the kerb $30 firmer at $1,528.
The September/October spread widened to an $80 backwardation from $65 on Tuesday and the cash/threes came out to $100/$110.
The market is still trying to puzzle out China's position after reports of huge short positions held by Chinese smelters.
One trader said on Wednesday that Far East selling came in at the highs while other traders have spoken of buying coming from the same origin in recent days.
Nickel lost more ground, failing to defend the $7,180 support level and falling $100 to a low of $7,160, where it closed.
Next support was pegged at $7,100 and $7,010.
Copper edged higher, but was capped again by stubborn resistance at $2,300, ending $13 firmer at $2,298.
The cash/threes narrowed again by a couple of dollars to a $22/$27 backwardation.
Lead sulked near 22-month lows hit on Tuesday, keeping to a tight range and closing the session $1 firmer at $606.
Trade buying has been seen on the lows, while some players were betting on a bounce and buying upside calls in the morning, traders said.
But analysts say lead looks weak and more tests of the downside could be on the cards after a consolidation period. Next support is charted at $589, $580 and $572.
Tin was dull, adding $5 to $5,590 and alloy was last at $1,525/35, up about $10. --Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
